Given two $n\times n$ matrices $M$ and $N,$ we have

$$
det(MN)=det(M)\cdot det(N).
$$

In our case, this gives

$$
det(C)=det[\begin{aligned}6 & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot det[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 5 \\ -6 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

We can compute the required determinants as follows:

- For the first determinant, we can compute it using a Laplace expansion across the $3$rd row.

- For the second determinant, we can compute it using a Laplace expansion down the $2$nd column.

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}det(C) & =|\begin{aligned}6 & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}|\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 5 \\ -6 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|\cdot (-1)(-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(6-4)\cdot (-1)(12-5) \\  & =4\cdot (-7) \\  & =-28.\end{aligned}
$$
